findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime keys
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint routes optimized_pagination=true requests to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime". This class's get_item_key() calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on the datetime value, and value_from_cursor() returns the raw integer cursor instead of converting it back to a datetime. build_cursor() calls get_item_key() on every non-empty page, so the optimized branch raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime"); even if that were fixed, build_queryset() would compare a datetime column against an integer cursor value. Any optimized audit-log request with results will fail, and cursors are not interoperable with DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset branch passes negative bounds to Django QuerySet
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is left negative and passed to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds; they raise ValueError/AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported") rather than returning reverse-pagination results. A client can supply such a cursor, so the new advanced path produces a 500 instead of working. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid non-negative offset before slicing.

findings.title: Negative offsets are only partially clamped in BasePaginator
findings.body: The new shared BasePaginator logic clamps negative offsets only for forward cursors: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. A previous-page cursor with a negative offset still passes a negative bound to queryset[...] and raises. For a forward cursor with a negative offset, the query is silently shifted to row 0 while build_cursor() still receives the original negative cursor offset, so _build_next_values()/_build_prev_values() can generate inconsistent offsets and a has_prev flag for a page that does not exist. Negative offsets should be normalized or rejected up front instead of being handled differently by direction.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized audit-log pagination path
findings.body: No tests were added for OptimizedCursorPaginator or for the new optimized_pagination branch. A simple test with AuditLogEntry rows and order_by="-datetime" would have caught the datetime TypeError, and a test with a negative-offset cursor would have caught the unsupported Django negative slicing. Without coverage this new privileged code path can ship completely non-functional while the existing DateTimePaginator path continues to pass tests.
